30	does NOT implement is gated off, because the batched Program-Buffer sweep
31	faults (cmderr=3) on a single over-claimed CSR.
32

37

46

58	inventory == matrix == ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`), so a CSR added to
59	the wire format without a disposition (or vice versa) fails loudly. New
60	transported CSRs are one X-macro line in `state_abi.h`
61	(`HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST` / `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`); every consumer
62	(plugin drain, restore, drain re-read, verify) iterates the same list.

65

67	repo's `src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` (address -> gate) and bind the gate to a
68	`_NDS_*` config macro in `andes_caps_config.hpp` (absent macro reads as

1	# Engine registration: per-engine, per-config test completeness
2	
3	andesim ships commercially. "The transport machinery is tested" is not the
4	same as "THIS engine build's CSR set is tested" -- every engine can differ
5	in its CSR set, and the same core built with a different config differs
6	again. Registration turns "nothing missed" from a convention into a set of
7	checks that fail.
8	
9	## Identity: an engine build = (core, config)
10	
11	The registration key is the engine name plus a short hash of the BUILD
12	`config.inc` (`build/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc` -- the file Phase 0
13	already reads). Layout in the andesim repo:
14	
15	```
16	tests/engines/<engine>-<confighash8>/
17	├── engine.env          # engine name, QEMU -cpu pairing, march, vlen, priv levels
18	├── csr_manifest.csv    # deliverable 1
19	└── fixtures/           # deliverable 3 (generated)
20	```
21	
22	A rebuilt config produces a different hash -> a different directory -> the
23	guard (deliverable 4) refuses to run the engine against the old artifacts.
24	Nothing about "same core, new config" can be silently reused.
25	
26	## Deliverable 1: the CSR manifest
27	
28	One row per spec-inventory CSR (all of them, not just transported ones):
29	
30	```
31	addr,name,access,exists_cond,implemented,transported,gate_or_disposition,reset_value
32	0x7D1,mcountermask_m,MRW,PMNDS&misa[20],no,no,UMODE(off),-
33	0x7CF,mcounterinten,MRW,PMNDS,yes,yes,PERF_MONITOR,0x0
34	...
35	```
36	
37	Column sources -- each answers a different question and they must agree:
38	- `exists_cond`: the SPA (per-CSR IM Requirement / Table 13) -- Phase 1.
39	- `implemented`: EMPIRICAL -- the probe (below), never inferred from QEMU.
40	- `transported`: the caps verdict (`--describe andes_csrs` of THIS binary).
41	- `reset_value`: EMPIRICAL -- from the probe or the reset-baseline capture
42	  file (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/*.bin` is a `hybrid_state_v1`; parse with
43	  the ABI struct). This IS the engine's reset value table: generated,
44	  reviewed by a human once against the spec's reset column (IM/DC fields
45	  will differ from the spec -- that is expected and fine), then committed.
46	
47	## Deliverable 2: the both-direction completeness check
48	
49	- **Over-claim** (caps says yes, RTL says no): already caught empirically --
50	  the cold-cache capture's CSR sweep faults and names the CSR. Keep a
51	  cold-cache hybrid run in the engine's registered test set so this is a
52	  TEST, not an incident.
53	- **Under-claim** (RTL has it, caps gates it off -- the silent state-loss
54	  case): script it from the manifest. Every row with
55	  `exists_cond == true against this config.inc` (or `implemented == yes`
56	  from the probe) must have `transported == yes` OR a named `EXCL_*`
57	  disposition from the coverage matrix. A row with neither FAILS. This is
58	  the "nothing missed" enforcement -- no human list-checking.
59	
60	**The probe.** A checked read of every inventory CSR on the halted,
61	freshly reset hart (the DM mirrors an unimplemented CSR as a cmderr, which
62	`read_register_64_checked` reports as nullopt) yields the implemented set
63	plus reset values in one pass (~232 reads, seconds of sim time). If the sim
64	binary has no probe mode yet, building one is part of the FIRST
65	registration -- it is a small loop over the inventory using existing
66	helpers; do it test-first like everything else. Skip EXCL_SIDEFX rows
67	(reads with side effects) by policy.
68	
69	## Deliverable 3: generated per-engine fixtures
70	
71	Write-survival tests must exist per engine and must come from a GENERATOR
72	keyed by the manifest, not from hand-written files -- hand-written sets rot

# Engine registration: per-engine, per-config test completeness

andesim ships commercially. "The transport machinery is tested" is not the
same as "THIS engine build's CSR set is tested" -- every engine can differ
in its CSR set, and the same core built with a different config differs
again. Registration turns "nothing missed" from a convention into a set of
checks that fail.

## Identity: an engine build = (core, config)

The registration key is the engine name plus a short hash of the BUILD
`config.inc` (`build/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc` -- the file Phase 0
already reads). Layout in the andesim repo:

```
tests/engines/<engine>-<confighash8>/
├── engine.env          # engine name, QEMU -cpu pairing, march, vlen, priv levels
├── csr_manifest.csv    # deliverable 1
└── fixtures/           # deliverable 3 (generated)
```

A rebuilt config produces a different hash -> a different directory -> the
guard (deliverable 4) refuses to run the engine against the old artifacts.
Nothing about "same core, new config" can be silently reused.

## Deliverable 1: the CSR manifest

One row per spec-inventory CSR (all of them, not just transported ones):

```
addr,name,access,exists_cond,implemented,transported,gate_or_disposition,reset_value
0x7D1,mcountermask_m,MRW,PMNDS&misa[20],no,no,UMODE(off),-
0x7CF,mcounterinten,MRW,PMNDS,yes,yes,PERF_MONITOR,0x0
...
```

Column sources -- each answers a different question and they must agree:
- `exists_cond`: the SPA (per-CSR IM Requirement / Table 13) -- Phase 1.
- `implemented`: EMPIRICAL -- the probe (below), never inferred from QEMU.
- `transported`: the caps verdict (`--describe andes_csrs` of THIS binary).
- `reset_value`: EMPIRICAL -- from the probe or the reset-baseline capture
  file (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/*.bin` is a `hybrid_state_v1`; parse with
  the ABI struct). This IS the engine's reset value table: generated,
  reviewed by a human once against the spec's reset column (IM/DC fields
  will differ from the spec -- that is expected and fine), then committed.

## Deliverable 2: the both-direction completeness check

- **Over-claim** (caps says yes, RTL says no): already caught empirically --
  the cold-cache capture's CSR sweep faults and names the CSR. Keep a
  cold-cache hybrid run in the engine's registered test set so this is a
  TEST, not an incident.
- **Under-claim** (RTL has it, caps gates it off -- the silent state-loss
  case): script it from the manifest. Every row with
  `exists_cond == true against this config.inc` (or `implemented == yes`
  from the probe) must have `transported == yes` OR a named `EXCL_*`
  disposition from the coverage matrix. A row with neither FAILS. This is
  the "nothing missed" enforcement -- no human list-checking.

**The probe.** A checked read of every inventory CSR on the halted,
freshly reset hart (the DM mirrors an unimplemented CSR as a cmderr, which
`read_register_64_checked` reports as nullopt) yields the implemented set
plus reset values in one pass (~232 reads, seconds of sim time). If the sim
binary has no probe mode yet, building one is part of the FIRST
registration -- it is a small loop over the inventory using existing
helpers; do it test-first like everything else. Skip EXCL_SIDEFX rows
(reads with side effects) by policy.

## Deliverable 3: generated per-engine fixtures

Write-survival tests must exist per engine and must come from a GENERATOR
keyed by the manifest, not from hand-written files -- hand-written sets rot
and miss CSRs. For each transported read/write CSR: write a distinctive
value before the ROI (proves resume restores it) and inside the ROI (proves
drain captures it), assert via the drained state and `--verify`.

The generator needs a per-CSR safe-write policy, because blind writes to
control CSRs break the run (mcache_ctl flips caches, milmb/mdlmb move local
memory, mhsp_ctl arms stack protection). Policy tiers:
- plain state (scratch-like, masks, event selects): write a full
  distinctive pattern;
- WARL-constrained: write within a reviewed mask;
- dangerous control CSRs: skip-list with a comment saying why -- the
  round-trip of these is still covered by --verify on real workload values.
The policy table is reviewed once and committed next to the generator.

## Deliverable 4: the registration guard

A script that cross-checks: every engine `./andesim list engines` reports
must have a `tests/engines/<engine>-<confighash8>/` whose hash matches the
CURRENT binary's config.inc, with a manifest and generated fixtures
present. Unregistered or stale-hash engines fail with "run the bring-up
registration". Wire it next to the existing coverage guard so CI runs both.

## Matrix runner

The full 47-fixture suite stays on the default engines (wall-time). Every
REGISTERED engine runs its own core set on every suite run: the probe
check, its generated CSR fixtures, a cold-cache hybrid run (the sweep
validator), and one --verify run. `run_e2e.sh` takes the engine axis from
the registration dirs, so adding a registration automatically adds its
tests -- no runner edit, nothing to forget.

# Engine registration: CSR test artifacts required to ship a new vsim engine

Answer: four deliverables per engine BUILD -- (1) a CSR manifest, (2) a
both-direction completeness check, (3) generated per-engine write-survival
fixtures, (4) a registration guard -- all keyed by the hash of the build's
`config.inc`, so a rebuild with a different config is a NEW registration by
construction and can never silently reuse the old artifacts.

## 1. The identity: an engine build = (core, config)

The engine's compiled-in config is the only truth about which CSRs it
implements. The registration key is the engine name plus a short hash
(first 8 hex chars) of the BUILD-directory config:

```
$VSIM_BIN_DIR/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc
```

Concretely, with today's `config.env` (`VSIM_BIN_DIR=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build`):

- `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/Vax45mpv_premium/obj_sc/config.inc`
- `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/Vax46mpv_advanced/obj_sc/config.inc`

Use the build copy, never the `external/` source tree (it can differ from
what was actually built), and never QEMU's view (its gdbstub advertises CSRs
the vsim RTL does not implement; sweeping one stalls or faults the Debug
Module).

Artifact layout in the andesim repo:

```
tests/engines/<engine>-<confighash8>/
|-- engine.env          # engine name, QEMU -cpu pairing, march, vlen, priv levels
|-- csr_manifest.csv    # deliverable 1
`-- fixtures/           # deliverable 3 (generated)
```

Rebuilding the same core with a different config changes the hash, which
changes the directory name, which makes the guard (deliverable 4) refuse to
run the engine against the old artifacts. "Same core, new config" cannot be
silently reused -- reuse is impossible by construction, not by review
discipline.

## 2. Deliverable 1: the CSR manifest (`csr_manifest.csv`)

One row per spec-inventory CSR -- ALL of them (the current inventory,
`tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv`, has 232 CSRs from the SPA), not just
the transported ones:

```
addr,name,access,exists_cond,implemented,transported,gate_or_disposition,reset_value
0x7D1,mcountermask_m,MRW,PMNDS&misa[20],no,no,UMODE(off),-
0x7CF,mcounterinten,MRW,PMNDS,yes,yes,PERF_MONITOR,0x0
```

Each column comes from a DIFFERENT source, and they must agree:

- `exists_cond`: the SPA spec (per-CSR IM Requirement / Table 13) --
  Phase 1 output.
- `implemented`: EMPIRICAL, from the probe (section 3) -- never inferred
  from QEMU.
- `transported`: the caps verdict of THIS binary --
  `sim_<engine> --describe` emits the `andes_csrs` JSON list the engine
  compiled in (`src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` + `andes_caps_config.hpp` in the
  vsim repo).
- `reset_value`: EMPIRICAL -- from the probe or the reset-baseline capture
  (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/*.bin` is a `hybrid_state_v1` struct; parse with
  the ABI header `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`). This IS the engine's reset
  value table: generated, reviewed once by a human against the spec's reset
  column (IM/DC fields will differ from the spec -- expected and fine), then
  committed.

## 3. Deliverable 2: the both-direction completeness check

"Nothing missed" has two failure directions; each needs its own check.

**Over-claim** (caps says yes, RTL says no): the batched Program-Buffer CSR
sweep faults (cmderr=3) on a single over-claimed CSR and bisects to name it.
This matters because the tolerant abstract-command path MASKS this bug: a
faulting read mirrors as zero, QEMU drains zero too, and `--verify` falsely
matches. A cold-cache hybrid run exercises the sweep via the reset-baseline
capture -- keep one in the engine's registered test set so an over-claim is
a TEST failure, not a field incident.

**Under-claim** (RTL implements it, caps gates it off -- the silent
state-loss case): script it from the manifest. Every row whose
`exists_cond` evaluates true against this `config.inc` (or whose probe says
`implemented == yes`) must have `transported == yes` OR a named `EXCL_*`
disposition from the coverage matrix (`tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv`).
A row with neither FAILS the script. No human list-checking.

**The probe** that feeds both: a checked read of every inventory CSR on the
halted, freshly reset hart. The DM mirrors an unimplemented CSR as a
cmderr, which `read_register_64_checked` reports as nullopt -- so one pass
(~232 reads, seconds of sim time) yields the implemented set AND the
empirical reset values. EXCL_SIDEFX rows (reads with side effects) are
skipped by policy. The sim binaries have no probe mode today (grep of
`src/hybrid/` and `main.cpp` in the vsim repo finds none); building it is
part of the FIRST registration -- a small loop over the inventory using the
existing DM helpers, done test-first.

## 4. Deliverable 3: generated per-engine write-survival fixtures

Write-survival tests must come from a GENERATOR keyed by the manifest, not
from hand-written files. Today's CSR fixtures (`tests/fixtures/
rt_csr_survival.S`, `rt_m_ext_counters.S`, `rt_m_ext_trigcause.S`) are
hand-written and engine-generic; hand-written sets rot and miss CSRs when a
new engine claims a different set.

For each transported read/write CSR the generator emits: a distinctive
write BEFORE the ROI (proves resume restores it into the vsim hart) and one
INSIDE the ROI (proves drain captures it), asserted via the drained state
and `--verify`.

The generator needs a per-CSR safe-write policy, because blind writes to
control CSRs break the run (`mcache_ctl` flips caches, `milmb`/`mdlmb`
move local memory, `mhsp_ctl` arms stack protection). Three tiers:

- plain state (scratch-like, masks, event selects): full distinctive pattern;
- WARL-constrained: write within a reviewed mask;
- dangerous control CSRs: skip-list with a comment saying why -- their
  round-trip is still covered by `--verify` on real workload values.

The policy table is reviewed once and committed next to the generator.

## 5. Deliverable 4: the registration guard

A script that cross-checks: every engine that `./andesim list engines`
reports (driver F2 discovery, `driver/cmd_list.cpp:list_engines`) must have
a `tests/engines/<engine>-<confighash8>/` directory whose hash matches the
CURRENT binary's `config.inc`, with the manifest and generated fixtures
present. An unregistered engine, or one whose hash went stale after a
rebuild, fails with "run the bring-up registration". Wire it next to the
existing coverage guard (`tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py` /
`test_csr_coverage_complete.sh`) so CI runs both.

## 6. How the checks compose ("nothing missed" as machine invariants)

Layered guards, each catching what the others cannot:

1. `tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py` (exists today): inventory == matrix
   == ABI (`state_abi.h` X-macros `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST` /
   `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`). A CSR added to the wire format without a
   disposition, or vice versa, fails loudly. Engine-independent.
2. `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_caps_parity.sh` +
   `scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py` (exist today): the offline Python
   gate logic run on the engine's build `config.inc` must reproduce the
   built binary's `--describe andes_csrs` list -- offline config == compiled
   caps.
3. The under-claim script (deliverable 2, per engine): implemented-but-not-
   transported-and-not-excluded fails.
4. The cold-cache sweep run (deliverable 2, per engine): over-claims fault
   and name the CSR.
5. The registration guard (deliverable 4): unregistered or stale-hash
   engines cannot run at all.
6. Named verify exclusions live in ONE place
   (`driver/state_diff.cpp:andes_verify_excluded`, currently e.g.
   `msp_bound`/`msp_base`, `milmb`/`mdlmb`, `mip`), each with a comment
   naming the engine-reset divergence. Exclusion is only for
   engine-implementation artifacts, never to hide a transport bug.

Rebuild-with-different-config is covered by check 5: the new `config.inc`
hashes differently, the old `tests/engines/` dir no longer matches, and
every engine-scoped artifact (manifest, probe results, fixtures) must be
regenerated and re-reviewed under the new key.

## 7. Matrix runner integration

The full ~47-fixture suite stays on the default engines (wall-time). Every
REGISTERED engine runs its own core set on every suite run: the probe
check, its generated CSR fixtures, one cold-cache hybrid run (the sweep
validator), and one `--verify` run. `scripts/run_e2e.sh` takes the engine
axis from the registration dirs -- today it hardcodes a canonical default
engine plus an S/U special case for the priv fixtures, so this is a change
to make during first registration. After that, adding a registration
automatically adds its tests: no runner edit, nothing to forget.

## 8. Current state and first-registration work list

Exists today (andesim repo):

- `tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` (232 CSRs), `csr_coverage.csv`,
  `check_coverage.py`, `test_csr_coverage_complete.sh`
- `scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py`, `classify_csr_coverage.py`,
  `config_inc_to_andes_caps.py`, `render_csr_matrix.py`
- `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_caps_parity.sh`
- `driver/state_diff.cpp` named exclusions; reset-baseline cache under
  `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/`
- vsim side: `--describe` with `andes_csrs`, caps gates in
  `src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` / `andes_caps_config.hpp`

Missing -- to build (test-first) as part of the FIRST registration:

1. `tests/engines/` layout + `engine.env` convention (does not exist yet).
2. The probe mode in the sim binary (checked read of the full inventory on
   the reset hart).
3. The manifest generator (probe output + `--describe` + spec inventory ->
   `csr_manifest.csv`).
4. The under-claim completeness script.
5. The fixture generator + reviewed safe-write policy table.
6. The registration guard script, wired next to the coverage guard.
7. `run_e2e.sh` engine axis from registration dirs.

Then register both currently built engines (`ax45mpv_premium`,
`ax46mpv_advanced`) as the first two entries; any future build -- new core
OR new config of an old core -- follows the same recipe and is refused by
the guard until its artifacts exist.
